mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate compresses equity valuations through increased discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as measured by the FEDFUNDS series.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (Rank IC > -0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate broad-based consumer demand weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict negative returns: 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals supply chain disruptions and reduced manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion, when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% in 3 months, S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC between RSAFS and 5-day forward returns is not significantly positive (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 4.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting restrictive monetary policy that depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 4.0%, S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous slowdown in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, reducing consumer confidence and corporate hiring, driving negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise fails to predict negative returns: 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a rapid FEDFUNDS increase signals aggressive policy, raising borrowing costs and reducing corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, when FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a month, S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.
